info.title: Mesadesk API
info.description:
REST API for the Mesadesk: the manufacturing value chain from customer
inquiry through order, production plan, shift logbook, quality inspection,
finished-goods stock and dispatch, plus the complaint/CAPA loop that closes
back onto it.

**This document is generated from the running server.** Paths, methods, request
bodies, authentication and the permission each route is gated on are read from
the live Express router stack and the Zod schemas that validate the requests, so
they cannot drift from what is enforced.

### Conventions

- Base path `/api`. Request and response bodies are JSON.
- Every failure uses the same envelope: `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details?" } }`.
  Branch on `error.code`, which is stable; `message` is for humans.
- Writes are validated with Zod and return `422` with a field-level error map on failure.
- Lifecycle transitions are their own endpoints (`/orders/{id}/cancel`,
  `/logbooks/{id}/submit`, `/capas/{id}/close`) and are transactional where they
  touch several tables.
- Every request is scoped to the caller's organization; there is no way to read
  or write another tenant's rows.
- Response schemas come from the Prisma datamodel. Where an endpoint includes a
  relation, the nested object may carry only the fields that endpoint selects.

### Authorization

Authentication establishes *who* you are; each route additionally requires a
feature permission, listed in its description as **Requires permission**. Roles
map to permissions server-side — the client's own checks are cosmetic only.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Liveness and the caller’s own identity.

tags.name: Sales
tags.description: Customers, inquiries, quotations and sales orders — the head of the value chain.

tags.name: Planning
tags.description: Scheduling confirmed orders onto a machine, shift and date.

tags.name: Manufacturing
tags.description: Shift logbooks and the templates that shape them. A logbook may only be opened against a scheduled plan.

tags.name: Quality
tags.description: Roll inspection. A pass books finished-goods stock, which is what makes a roll dispatchable.

tags.name: Dispatch
tags.description: Shipping produced orders: dispatch record, invoice and the finished-goods stock movement.

tags.name: Inventory
tags.description: Ledger-derived stock balances plus raw-material receive and issue.

tags.name: CAPA
tags.description: Customer complaints against dispatched batches and the corrective/preventive actions that close them out.

tags.name: Maintenance
tags.description: Machine registry and the preventive maintenance schedule.

tags.name: Dashboard
tags.description: Aggregated KPIs for the per-role home screens.

tags.name: Administration
tags.description: Employees, roles and per-employee screen access.

tags.name: Onboarding
tags.description: Create a new organization and its first owner account.

tags.name: MesaLeads
tags.description: Configurable customer questionnaires, lead qualification, pipeline and follow-up.

tags.name: Legacy
tags.description: The data.json blob store still backing domains not yet migrated to Postgres. Being retired domain by domain.

get.description: Unauthenticated. Returns as soon as the process is serving; it does not check the database.

auth.description: dev = x-dev-user picker; authjs = Google OAuth + per-user password (Postgres sessions)

post.description: Verifies User.passwordHash, creates an Auth.js Session row, and sets the httpOnly session cookie. The response keeps the selected membership fields at user level for backward compatibility and includes all selectable organization contexts. Services include only active assignments backed by an active global service; suspended organizations receive no services. Google OAuth uses /auth/signin/google instead.

parameters.name: x-org
parameters.description: Optionally select one owned, non-inactive organization membership by id or slug after the credentials are verified.

200.description: The selected membership, every organization context and their usable services; session cookie is set.

401.description: - `invalid_credentials` — Email or password is wrong, or the user has no passwordHash.

403.description:
- `no_membership` — The email is not an active organization member.
- `organization_not_available` — x-org does not identify a non-inactive membership owned by the authenticated user.

429.description: - `rate_limited` — The IP, account, or IP-account attempt budget is exhausted.

post.description: Verifies the email and password, then requires the identity to be explicitly listed in ONBOARDING_ALLOWED_EMAILS and to hold at least one active admin membership. The Auth.js database Session and httpOnly cookie are created only after both authentication and platform authorization succeed.

200.description: The authorized platform administrator context; session cookie is set.

400.description: - `invalid_body` — Email or password is missing or outside the accepted bounds.

401.description: - `invalid_credentials` — Email or password is wrong, or the user has no passwordHash.

403.description: - `platform_admin_required` — Credentials are valid but the identity is not allowlisted or has no active admin membership. No session is created.

429.description: - `rate_limited` — The IP, account, or IP-account attempt budget is exhausted.

get.summary: Restore a cookie session for the landing page
get.description: Resolves only a real Auth.js database-session cookie and never the DEV_AUTH fallback identity. With no cookie it returns `{ "user": null }`, allowing a fresh local visit to remain on the two-login entry screen. Send x-org with an owned organization id or slug to restore that tenant.

parameters.name: x-org
parameters.description: Optionally restore one owned, non-inactive organization membership by id or slug.

200.description: The authenticated organization context, or a null user when no session cookie is present.

401.description: - `invalid_token` — The supplied session cookie is unknown or expired; the cookie is cleared.

403.description:
- `no_membership` — The session user has no non-inactive organization membership.
- `organization_not_available` — x-org does not identify a non-inactive membership owned by the session user.

post.description: Deletes the Session row for the cookie (if any) and clears the Auth.js session cookie.
